title: Coffee and Walnut Cake
subtitle: a classic British layer cake with coffee buttercream and walnuts
excerpt: Coffee and walnut cake is the most popular cake in British cafes and tea rooms. The sponge is flavoured with strong coffee, layered with coffee buttercream, and decorated with walnut halves. It is an elegant, unfussy cake.
sourceNotes: A British tea room classic. Coffee became a common baking flavour in Britain during the 20th century.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze unfrosted sponge layers. Frost and decorate on the day.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Bake layers the day before. Make buttercream and assemble on the day.

content.text: Dissolve the instant coffee in the minimum amount of hot water -- this concentrates the flavour. A tablespoon of water is enough. Add it to both the cake batter and the buttercream. The walnut pieces can go into the batter as well as on top if you want a stronger nutty flavour throughout.

items.prepNote: use 75g walnuts, roughly chopped -- plus extra halves for decoration
use 2 tsp instant coffee dissolved in 1 tbsp hot water -- for both batter and buttercream
use 200g unsalted butter, softened -- for the coffee buttercream
use 200g icing sugar for the buttercream

content.text: Dissolve 2 tsp instant coffee in 1 tbsp hot water. Set aside to cool.

Heat the oven to 180C. Grease and line two 20cm round tins. Beat the butter, caster sugar, eggs, flour, baking powder, milk, and half the coffee mixture together until smooth. Fold in the chopped walnuts.
Divide between the tins. Bake for 22 to 25 minutes until risen and springing back. Cool in tins for 5 minutes, then turn out.
Make the buttercream: beat the softened butter until pale. Sift in the icing sugar. Add the remaining coffee mixture and beat until smooth.
Sandwich the cooled layers with half the buttercream. Spread the rest over the top. Decorate with walnut halves.

items.symptom: Buttercream is too sweet and cloying
items.cause: Coffee not strong enough to balance the sugar.
items.fix: Use a stronger coffee solution -- 3 tsp in 1 tbsp water. The coffee bitterness is what balances the sweetness.

items.symptom: Walnuts sink to the bottom of the cake
items.cause: Pieces too heavy for the batter.
items.fix: Chop walnuts finely rather than roughly. Smaller pieces stay suspended. Alternatively, toss them in a little flour before adding.

content.text: Coffee and walnut cake is the quintessential British tea room cake. It appears under glass domes on cafe counters from Edinburgh to Cornwall. The combination of mild coffee, buttery sponge, and earthy walnut is one of the great flavour pairings in British baking. It is reliable, crowd-pleasing, and never goes out of fashion.
